native_reference.getStatus_fact: VirtualMachine.java:808-829 catches RemoteException and returns STATUS_STOPPED; raw STOPPED is not independent proof of exact native owner release. Caller-side exception handling cannot recover this suppressed failure.
native_reference.stop_fact: VirtualMachine.stop is blocking and only drops binding after binder stop returns; native kill has a five-second condition wait followed by unbounded exit/tracing joins, and concurrent shutdown may wait without a deadline.
native_reference.model_policy: Raw STOPPED, binder failure and unconfirmed status preserve ownership as UNKNOWN. Only separately trusted exact-owner stop confirmation or verified pending-without-native settlement releases lease. No such independent production confirmation API is implemented here.
native_reference.scope: Separate AOSP reference for lower-layer shutdown behavior, not installed donor byte equivalence. Exact donor Java behavior is pinned separately and differs on stop failures.

source_counterexamples: Source-permitted service-first Ready/start ordering stops service before separately modeled worker creates native VM.
Worker-first interleaving keeps coverage; failure is not claimed inevitable.
Source-constrained late Error publication plus actual checkStopSelf and actual reset retain dummy native reference with no service.
Actual start returns before service reconciliation when already Running.
Actual donor getStatus hides modeled remote failure as STOPPED; stop based on that ambiguous status throws and drops binding; fake native remains alive only with modeled cleanup stop failure too.
Actual donor stop drops binding after modeled native stop and subsequent cleaner stop both fail; successful native stop separately completes and drops binding.
licensing_scope: Own host stand-ins/model are Apache-2.0. Donor method bodies are extracted only into temporary local test output; no donor class or APK is bundled by these candidate files. Donor licensing/signing authority is not inferred from older AOSP. Pinned AOSP reference files retain their existing notices and are not redistributed here.
limitations: This is an executable host contract/model, not a production APK patch, instrumentation, Android lifecycle test or runtime fix.

Seven simple reconstructed donor methods compile unchanged against explicit stand-ins. Android scheduling, coroutine execution, service promotion and native VM are modeled. Error transition is constrained by pinned source text, not a compilable production callback.
No matching donor new2 Kotlin checkout, platform signing integration or independent native-stop confirmation mechanism is supplied.
Current installed APK byte equivalence was established by main lane; this test verifies only saved inputs. Source counterexamples do not establish which path, if any, caused prior cached-parent exit.
Pending-start settlement, generation serialization, native-create admission and trusted stop confirmation are required production contracts, not APIs added to current donor app.
Model never disables CPU policy, claims low CPU, invents cleanup on timeout, grants a permanent FGS exemption or solves sustained child CPU.
No production/native build, APK repack/sign/install or device operation was performed.
Model foreground acknowledgement and exact-owner confirmation are trusted inputs; it does not simulate every Android policy action or process death after acknowledgement.
